# One codebase for web, iOS and Android: evaluation table

Date 05/10/2026. Answers question FE-09 of `spec/frontend-brainstorm-log.md`. This
version was re-evaluated once on the same day; the first version is in section 7.

## 1. Conclusion (after re-evaluation)

Given the new condition of the product owner, best performance on every device including
phones, the direction to choose is **React Native with Expo**: one TypeScript codebase that runs
natively on iOS and Android, and renders real HTML on the web through React Native for Web.
This is the only one of the three directions in which no device is scored below 4 for performance.

- **Capacitor** still has the highest total score thanks to the web side, but on phones it runs
  the web UI inside a native shell, scoring only 3 for performance, and so fails the new condition.
- **Flutter** runs best on phones, but on the web it must download a renderer of about 1,5 MB
  and draw onto a canvas, so the web scores only 2 and is weak on accessibility.

## 2. Two adjustments by the product owner

The product owner's words, 05/10/2026: "I am not sure I will use typescript or node for
the backend, because we have deleted the whole app folder and rewritten the FO set from scratch, then I will
do the same for the BO set, later I will have to roll out many internal agent functions for
the app, so I will need 1 more stable framework for the backend, to be designed later. In the
meantime, the app must be designed to run with the best perfomance on all devices,
including mobile".

1. **The back-end language is not settled.** The decision `BD-01` (TypeScript on Node) is
   reopened; the back-end will be redesigned from scratch after the front-end. So the criterion "sharing
   TypeScript with the back-end" is dropped from the table. The API contract written in zod is still what
   is handed over to the back-end, whichever language the back-end uses.
2. **Best performance on every device, including phones.** It becomes a mandatory
   condition: any direction with a device that performs poorly is dropped before total scores are considered.

## 3. The re-evaluation table

Scale 1 to 5, 5 is the best. Scores are the writer's evaluation based on the facts in
section 4. Performance scores are not yet measured on a real device; section 6 proposes how to measure.

| Criterion | Capacitor | React Native with Expo | Flutter |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stability | 4. Version 8 supported since 08/12/2025, clear policy | 4. New Architecture by default since 0.76, six releases a year; Expo SDK 57 supports React Native for Web 0.21, although this web project is a community one | 4. Stable releases by quarter; the web side has had a major change (HTML renderer dropped 02/12/2024) |
| Expanding with little effort | 5. One UI for all three platforms | 4. One codebase; heavy web-only screens written in the DOM in the same repo | 4. One Dart codebase for all three platforms; only 5,9% of developers use Dart (TypeScript 43,6%) |
| Ease of maintenance | 4. One set of web technologies | 3. Upgrading React Native about once every two months (Expo takes most of the load); two sets of components (native and DOM) | 4. One consistent set of widgets; dense tables depend on a commercial library |
| Performance on phones | 3. Web UI in a native shell | 4. Native views, JSI removes the asynchronous bridge | 5. Impeller renderer, precompiled shaders |
| Performance on the web | 5. Real HTML, small bundle | 4. Real HTML, with one extra conversion layer | 2. Downloads about 1,5 MB more for the renderer, draws onto a canvas |
| Fit for Metis on the web (WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility, DOM-measuring gates, dense tables) | 5. Keeps the design and the six gates as they are | 4. Real HTML with ARIA attributes so the gates run on the web; the tree table and the drawing canvas are written in the DOM for the web | 2. The semantics tree for screen readers exists only when switched on; DOM measurement and axe-core cannot be used as designed |
| **Mandatory condition: no device below 4 for performance** | **Fails** (phone 3) | **Passes** | **Fails** (web 2) |
| Total of 6 criteria, for reference only | 26 | 23 | 21 |

Kotlin with Compose Multiplatform is eliminated before scoring: web (Kotlin/Wasm) is only at
Beta level (section 4.4).

## 4. Facts by platform, with sources

All read on 05/10/2026.

### 4.1 Capacitor

- "a cross-platform native runtime that makes it easy to build performant mobile
  applications that run natively on iOS, Android"; "can be dropped into any existing
  modern JavaScript project"; device functions go through plugins. [Source: https://capacitorjs.com/docs]
- Version 8 is active, released 08/12/2025; requires iOS from 15.0, Android from 7.0. [Source: https://capacitorjs.com/docs/main/reference/support-policy]
- Apple App Review section 4.2: "Your app should include features, content, and UI that
  elevate it beyond a repackaged website." [Source: https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/]

### 4.2 React Native with Expo

- React Native latest version 0.87. [Source: https://reactnative.dev/versions]
- "As of React Native 0.76, the New Architecture is enabled by default"; JSI "removes
  the asynchronous bridge between JavaScript and native". [Source: https://reactnative.dev/architecture/landing-page]
- Expo SDK 57.0.0: React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3, iOS 16.4+, Android 7+, React
  Native Web 0.21.0; following the "six releases per year" cadence of React Native. [Source: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/]
- React Native for Web renders real HTML: `role` derives the semantic tag, supports `aria-*`
  per WAI-ARIA 1.2, `tabIndex` for keyboard focus. [Source: https://necolas.github.io/react-native-web/docs/accessibility/]
  No official statement of maintenance by Meta was found [UNKNOWN].
- Expo DOM components (`'use dom'`): on the web a normal React component, on
  phones it runs in a WebView, data passes back and forth asynchronously as JSON; Expo advises "using
  truly native views whenever possible". [Source: https://docs.expo.dev/guides/dom-components/]
- NativeWind (Tailwind layer for React Native): version v5 is "Pre-release". [Source: https://www.nativewind.dev/]
- The MSW mock server runs on iOS and Android through the package `@msw/react-native`, with the warning
  "Use this integration at your own risk". [Source: https://mswjs.io/docs/integrations/react-native]
- Expo guides automated testing on iOS and Android with Maestro, written as flow files in
  YAML with `launchApp`, `tapOn`, `assertVisible`, run through EAS Workflows. [Source: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/workflows/examples/e2e-tests/]

### 4.3 Flutter

- Stable version 3.47 (month 8/2026); quarterly schedule: 3.41, 3.44, 3.47, next 3.50. [Source: https://docs.flutter.dev/release/archive]
- The web still has two renderers, canvaskit and skwasm; the HTML renderer was dropped, the flag `--web-renderer` removed on
  02/12/2024; canvaskit "adds about 1.5MB in download size". [Source: https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/web/renderers ; https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/159314]
- Flutter web "is not suitable for static websites with text-rich flow-based content". [Source: https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/web/faq]
- A screen reader on the web sees the app only when the semantics tree is switched on by the hidden button
  "Enable accessibility" or by `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. [Source: https://docs.flutter.dev/ui/accessibility/assistive-technologies ; https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/174016]
- Impeller is the only renderer on iOS, the default on Android API 29 and above; the web still uses Skia. [Source: https://docs.flutter.dev/perf/impeller]
- Syncfusion Flutter DataGrid runs on the web too, with screen reader support; it is a "commercial package". [Source: https://pub.dev/packages/syncfusion_flutter_datagrid]

### 4.4 Kotlin Multiplatform and Compose Multiplatform

- Compose Multiplatform: Android, iOS, desktop at Stable level; web (Kotlin/Wasm) at Beta level. [Source: https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/supported-platforms.html]

### 4.5 Talent pool

- Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, language usage rates (all respondents, then
  professionals): JavaScript 66% and 68,8%; TypeScript 43,6% and 48,8%; Kotlin 10,8% and 11,5%;
  Dart 5,9% and 6,1%. [Source: https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/technology]

## 5. If React Native with Expo is chosen, what the approved design changes

What is delivered stays the same: the shape of the shell and the overview screen, the mock data following the
zod contract, the typed translation layer, the intent of the six gates and the reverse tests. How it is built changes:

| Approved part | Change |
|---|---|
| Part 1, architecture | One Expo app running on web, iOS, Android replaces the Vite web app. The router is Expo Router. Mock server: MSW on the web; on phones use `@msw/react-native` or a mock data layer in `platform/` if that package proves unreliable. The `core/` folder stays the same |
| Part 1, design system | Built on the base components of React Native, receiving text through props as before. How tokens are attached (NativeWind, or StyleSheet with constants generated from `brand/tokens.css`) is settled in the spec; avoid NativeWind v5 while it is still a pre-release version. React Aria Components remain only for heavy web-only screens, not in the first batch |
| Part 2, shell and screen | The shape stays the same; the phone layout is at the same time the layout of the app |
| Part 3, translation layer | Stays the same |
| Part 3, six gates | On the web stays the same, because React Native for Web renders real HTML. On iOS and Android add Maestro flows that read the same screen contract, plus a check of accessibility labels. Fonts are loaded with expo-font, the SVG logo through react-native-svg |
| First batch | The overview screen runs on both the iOS Simulator and the Android Emulator, performance is measured on one mid-range Android device before sign-off |

## 6. What is uncertain and how to measure

- The performance scores of the three directions are evaluations, not yet measured. Proposal: in the first batch, measure the overview
  screen on a real device (app open time, frames while scrolling, time to show the figures)
  and record the numbers in the spec; if the numbers do not pass, go back to this table.
- Long-term maintenance of React Native for Web: no official source yet; Expo currently
  supports version 0.21 in SDK 57.
- `@msw/react-native` itself admits "at your own risk": needs to be tried early.

## 7. The first evaluation, now replaced

The first version also scored the criterion of sharing TypeScript with the back-end and did not yet have the condition
of performance on every device. Total scores then: Capacitor 26, React Native with Expo
22, Flutter 19, Kotlin with Compose Multiplatform 15; the recommendation then was Capacitor.
The two adjustments in section 2 changed the recommendation.
